title: BIOmarkers in Severe AsthMa Patients on Omalizumab Treatment
brief_summary: Eosinophil infiltration and degranulation in airways has been implicated in the pathology of asthma. Periostin is considered to be a marker of eosinophilic inflammation and is one of the highly expressed genes in epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts in asthma. Omalizumab is approved as add-on therapy in the treatment of severe allergic asthma. The aim of the study is to assess inflammatory biomarkers including: blood and sputum eosinophilia, periostin and IL-6 as long-term clinical outcomes of omalizumab therapy.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. positive history of atopy
2. serum total IgE level between 30 and 700 IU/ml
3. body weight not more than 150 kg
4. high dose of ICS and LABA
5. a documented history of 2-6 exacerbations requiring treatment with systemic corticosteroids ( with \>15 mg/day prednisone or other medications at similar dose, for at least 3 days).

Exclusion Criteria:

1. smoking
2. pregnancy
